text: Before delivering their devastating charge, the tongues of flame they unleash tear through the enemy line first.

The great trade ports of the eastern provinces often see a constant flow of imported and exported firearms, a fact that has left a deep mark on the tactical style of the troops garrisoned there. Before Nangau rose to become Cathay's industrial titan, older firearms produced in the workshops of Fuzhou and Beiqi already played their part in battles across Cathay. Even now, the doctrine of overwhelming firepower remains the dominant school of thought for the eastern frontier armies and navy.\\nThe firelance is a hybrid weapon combining firearm and polearm. Each of its barrels fires automatically in sequence after the previous discharge, sacrificing precision for tremendous bursts of power. Once the burning-hot barrels have been emptied, they become formidable weapons in close combat. Before the new Iron Hail Guns became widespread among Cathay's firearm troops, these quad-barreled firelances were once used extensively. Today, they remain the trump card of a select few elite shock cavalry.
The elite riders of the Chosen Vanguard Camp bear the weighty task of cutting through enemy lines, riding at the fore on the march and holding the flanks in formation.

Long before Cathay's unification, nomadic tribes from the north posed a grave threat to the central plains' rulers, their cataphract cavalry once a nightmare to the soldiers of the heartland. These elite riders called themselves the Bayara, meaning 'vanguard warriors.' From head to toe, both rider and steed, they were clad in brigandine-plated iron armor, granting them superior missile defense to lamellar armor while greatly reducing weight. This made them better suited for forward harassment, wearing down enemy forces through superior mobility. Now, at the call of the Dragon Emperor, former mortal enemies stand shoulder to shoulder against the ruin beyond the Azure Sea, together guarding Cathay's eternal peace.
The Dragon Spine Guardians are the elite garrison of Cathay's northern frontier, a living symbol of the Great Bastion. Only when every last one of them has fallen will the wall truly be under threat.

The Great Bastion, also known as the Dragon's Spine, is Cathay's impregnable colossal fortification along the northern frontier. This wall, personally overseen in its construction by the Dragon Emperor, stretches across province after province along the border, and for countless centuries has stood as the first line of defense against Chaos incursions from the north. Such a wonder was built through the combined effort of countless bricks and stones, together with tens of thousands of garrison soldiers unafraid of death. Though Jade Warrior units from different regions rotate through duty atop the Bastion, only the Dragon Spine Guardians remain stationed permanently upon this harsh and frozen frontier. As the core force of the Bastion's garrison, they are equipped with spiked shields and one-handed blunt weapons, true masters of holding the line.\\nWhether for material support or spiritual comfort, all their kin have settled with them near the Great Bastion. Despite the brutal conditions and the endless threat of Chaos, the Dragon Spine Guardians remain an unbreakable wall shielding all they hold dear.
The Beiwei warriors are well-equipped and high in morale; the great axes in their hands can easily cleave through enemy armor, making them the nightmare of cataphract cavalry.

Cathay's early standard weaponry emphasized nimble thrusting attacks, effective when large formations moved in coordination. But as the threat of Chaos tribes grew, the need for heavy blunt weapons capable of breaking armor increased in kind. Wielding such weapons demanded a physique and resolve far beyond the ordinary. Warriors selected from across the legions to form such a force became known as the Beiwei Army, equipped with heavy great axes and subjected to even harsher training.\\nOn the battlefield, the Beiwei Army fights with tight coordination and extraordinary courage; against cavalry, they sweep their great axes to sever the legs of horses, then cleave open the helmets of fallen riders with their blades. When the battle-hardened Beiwei Army appears at their side, Cathayan soldiers feel their spirits lifted, unleashing an even fiercer offensive. It is time to strike back to the north.
